name: openat
synopsis: int openat(int dirfd, const char *pathname, int flags, ...);
description: The openat() system call opens a file specified by pathname relative to a directory file descriptor. It provides a way to perform path resolution relative to an open directory, enhancing security against race conditions. The function returns a file descriptor for subsequent I/O operations.

parameters.name: dirfd
parameters.description: Directory file descriptor, or AT_FDCWD to use the current working directory

parameters.name: pathname
parameters.description: Pathname of the file to open, relative to dirfd

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags specifying access mode (e.g., O_RDONLY) and other options (e.g., O_CREAT)

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Mode for file creation if O_CREAT is specified in flags

return_value.success: Returns the new file descriptor (a nonnegative integer)
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error
